32 A proton enters the uniform electric field between two parallel vertical metal plates in a vacuum.
One plate is at a potential of 0 V and the other plate is at a potential of +10 V, as shown.
0 V

What is the initial change in the motion of the proton caused by the electric field, immediately
after the proton enters the field?
A
It begins to move downwards.
B
It begins to move upwards.
C
Its speed decreases.
D
Its speed increases.

hints: Notice the proton enters horizontally to the right through the $0\text{ V}$ plate toward the $+10\text{ V}$ plate.
Recall the uniform field between plates points from high potential to low potential, so determine whether it points left or right here.
Compare the direction of the force $F = qE$ on the positive proton with its initial velocity to decide if it speeds up, slows down or deflects sideways.
walkthrough: The proton enters moving horizontally to the right, perpendicular to the two vertical plates, with the left plate at $0\text{ V}$ and the right plate at $+10\text{ V}$.
In a uniform field, electric field direction is from high potential to low potential, so $E$ points from the $+10\text{ V}$ plate to the $0\text{ V}$ plate, which is to the left.
Force on a charge is $F = qE$ in the field direction for a positive charge, so the proton experiences a leftward force.
The initial velocity is rightward but the force and resulting acceleration are leftward, directly opposite the motion, with no vertical component.
An acceleration opposite to velocity causes deceleration, so the forward speed decreases immediately after entry. This is option C.

A.explanation: The electric force is horizontal, not vertical, so there is no initial vertical acceleration to start downward motion.

B.explanation: The electric force is horizontal, not vertical, so there is no initial vertical acceleration to start upward motion.

C.explanation: The field points left from $+10\text{ V}$ to $0\text{ V}$, so the force $F = qE$ on the positive proton points left, opposite its rightward velocity, and it slows down.

D.explanation: Speed would increase only if the force had a component along the velocity, but here the leftward force opposes the rightward motion.
